newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline, Zeneca up on Roche rumour.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline, Zeneca up on Roche rumour.

text.p: Shares in leading British drug companies SmithKline Beecham and Zeneca jumped on Wednesday amid unconfirmed market rumours that Swiss drugs giant Roche may be looking to merge with a foreign company.
SmithKline added 13-1/2p to 834-1/2p whilst Zeneca was up 33p at 16.75-1/2 stg.
"The drug stocks are climbing on speculation that Roche may either restructure or team up with a foreign partner," said one trader.
In Switzerland, certificates in Roche Holding AG leapt 11.7 percent in busy trade. Company officials declined to comment.
A spokeswoman for SmithKline Beecham said the company would not comment on market rumours. Zeneca also declined to comment.
London analysts said there appeared to be nothing to substantiate the rumours of a merger.

One analyst said the rumours suggested that Roche was about to announce the sale of one of its businesses, possibly the flavours and fragrances operations. "That would not justify the move" (in Roche certificates) he said.
Another analyst, who also asked not to be identified, said that "Roche has always been opportunistic in its acquisitions" and was keen to diversify from hospital-based products.

He added that Roche was keen to increase its exposure to general practitioner pharmaceuticals and while SmithKline Beecham could fill this gap, "you could make a reasonable case" for any of the top 20 worldwide drug companies.
Roche later said it had no plans to issue a statement today that would explain the stock rise.
